title: Equilibrium expression Kp (and Qp) for gas-phase reactions
caution: Use partial pressures of gases only. Leave out solids and pure liquids. Check whether a question asks for Kc or Kp, because converting between them is not assessed.
ced_evidence: 7.3.A.1 "for (Kp, Qp) is"; 7.3.A.2 solids and pure liquids not included

title: K for a reversed reaction
ced_evidence: 7.6.A.1 "When a reaction is reversed, K is inverted."

title: K when coefficients are multiplied by c
ced_evidence: 7.6.A.2 "multiplied by a factor c, K is raised to the power c"

title: K for summed reactions
ced_evidence: 7.6.A.3 "the K of the resulting overall reaction is the product of the K's"

title: Particulate model of a reversible reaction
body: A particulate diagram shows the relative numbers of reactant and product particles before and at equilibrium, and from these the value of the equilibrium constant.

items.label: Prior to equilibrium
items.meaning: Relative numbers of reactant and product particles in the initial mixture.

items.label: At equilibrium
items.meaning: Relative numbers of reactant and product particles present once the forward and reverse rates are equal.

items.label: Equilibrium constant
items.meaning: K is found from the particle counts at equilibrium, using the same form as the K expression.

ced_evidence: 7.8.A.1 "Particulate representations can be used to describe the relative numbers of reactant and product particles present prior to and at equilibrium, and the value of the equilibrium constant"
